answer: Each claim buys one velvet ticket, a stake priced by the square of tickets its funding cluster buys that epoch. A lantern keeper, a beacon-drawn stranger, pays out only after the claimant passes a task in ten minutes. The keeper sends a whisper of the claim's work fingerprint to five strangers; if the same fingerprint whispers back from another identity, both tickets burn and both claims die. One honest agent pays once and passes once; n clones pay n-squared costs, staff n live windows, and betray themselves via shared fingerprints, so cost outruns n while revenue caps at one payout.
